name: Gallery
summary: Six image gallery sections for the AhaSlides marketing sites, each a different way to show several photos across a page: a bento grid, a masonry wall, a snapping carousel with arrows and dots, a sticky stack that reveals step by step, two looping marquee rows, and tabs that crossfade between photos. Framework-free HTML and CSS bound to the shared --aha-* tokens, with the header, call to action and gutters of the Features section; the controls are icon-only <aha-button>s and Carousel dots wired by lib/marketing-motion.js. Each section has two backgrounds, White (the default) and Accent (add the class aha-gallery--accent).
highlights: Six layouts on one page, each with its own labelled preview and paste-and-run snippet

Every transition is timed with --aha-motion-* and --aha-ease-* tokens and stops under prefers-reduced-motion, print and data-aha-motion="off"; controls keep working with motion off, they just switch without the fade or smooth scroll
Nothing autoplays. The Marquee rows loop like the Logos strip, pause while hovered or focused, and carry a Pause button

Carousel and Tabbed images are keyboard reachable: Previous and Next are icon-only <aha-button>s, the dots are Carousel dots in 24 x 24 px buttons, and the tabs are WAI-ARIA tabs with arrow keys, Home and End

Every picture is a real of a DS placeholder with alt text to replace; cells with a fixed shape (bento squares, 4:3 carousel and marquee photos, 16:9 tabs and stack photos) fill with object-fit cover, so export the photo at that shape, and the masonry wall shows each photo whole at its own ratio
Same header (eyebrow, h2 title, lead), 48 px call-to-action gap and gutters (64, 24 and 16 px) as the Features section, and each section ends with one Sign up call to action
Each section is a container-query block: it steps down at 991 px and 767 px and tightens again below 480 px, wherever it sits
layoutsIntro: Each section is one gallery layout. They share one set of class names (aha-gallery), so the base CSS is pasted once and any number of layouts can sit in one page. Load lib/marketing-motion.js for the Carousel, Marquee rows and Tabbed images controls.

guidance.title: Choosing a gallery
guidance.intro: Every layout below has a White / Accent switch in its preview and a tab for each in its code.

points.title: By the photos you have
points.text: Photos of one shape: Bento grid (square) or Carousel (4:3). Photos of mixed shapes: Masonry, which never crops. One photo per audience or setting: Tabbed images. A short step-by-step story: Sticky stack. A big set of mood photos: Marquee rows.

points.title: One moving band per page
points.text: Use at most one looping band per page, the Marquee rows or the Hero image marquee, and never next to the Logos strip, so only one thing on the screen moves on its own.

points.title: Real photos, real alt text
points.text: Replace each placeholder with a real photo exported at its cell's shape, and write alt text that says what the photo shows. A photo that only decorates gets alt="".

points.title: Background
points.text: White is the default. Add aha-gallery--accent to lay the pale pink Accent background (bgAccent) over white when the section needs to stand apart; never place an Accent section next to another coloured one.

layouts.name: Bento grid
layouts.summary: A centred header, then five square photos in a bento: one large photo over two rows and columns, four small ones beside it, 16 px apart. From 767 px down it becomes two columns with the large photo on top. Every cell is square, so export each photo square and it fills its cell with no frame and no crop.
layouts.useFor: A quick visual summary of an event, a customer or a use case, in one screen.

layouts.name: Masonry
layouts.summary: A centred header, then eight photos of mixed shapes (landscape, portrait and wide) in three columns that each fill top to bottom, 24 px apart; two columns from 767 px down, 12 px apart below 480 px. Each photo shows whole at its own ratio, never cropped.

layouts.name: Carousel
layouts.summary: A centred header, then a row of captioned 4:3 photos, three in view at 1440 (one and a bit on a phone), that snaps photo by photo when swiped or scrolled. Below it the Previous and Next buttons (icon-only <aha-button>) and Carousel dots move it; the row itself is focusable, so arrow keys scroll it too. lib/marketing-motion.js wires the buttons and dots and scrolls smoothly unless reduced motion is on. Nothing moves on its own.
layouts.useFor: A longer set of photos (six or more) that should not take up the height of a grid, such as event recaps and customer stories.

layouts.name: Sticky stack
layouts.summary: A centred header, then four white cards (step, title, text and a 16:9 photo) that stick near the top of the screen as the page scrolls, each sliding over the one before and leaving a 16 px edge of it showing, so the steps reveal one by one. Pure CSS position: sticky: no script, no scroll-jacking, and the page scrolls at its normal speed; with reduced motion it behaves the same, as nothing animates. The docs preview does not scroll inside, so open the snippet in a page to see the stacking.
layouts.useFor: A short how-it-works story (three to five steps) where each step has its own picture.

layouts.name: Marquee rows
layouts.summary: A centred header, then two full-width rows of 4:3 photos sliding in opposite directions without end, the Logos loop applied to photos: each row is written twice (the copy hidden from assistive technology) and moves one set in 36 s (--aha-motion-viz-enter × 60), linear. Both rows pause while hovered or focused, and the Pause button (an icon-only <aha-button>, wired by lib/marketing-motion.js) stops them until pressed again. Under reduced motion, print or data-aha-motion="off" the rows stand still and the button is hidden.
layouts.useFor: A lively band of many photos between denser sections, such as a culture page or an event recap.

layouts.name: Tabbed images
layouts.summary: A centred header, then a row of tabs over one 16:9 photo; picking a tab crossfades to its photo (--aha-motion-viz-enter, --aha-ease-in-out). Working WAI-ARIA tabs: Tab reaches the selected tab, the arrow keys, Home and End move between tabs, wired by lib/marketing-motion.js. The tab style is the Features Tabs with screenshots one; the row scrolls sideways on a phone. Under reduced motion the photo switches with no fade.
layouts.useFor: One photo per audience, setting or use case, where the reader picks the one that fits them.
